biomarkers.name: See EXTRANODAL_MARGINAL_ZONE_MALT under B_CELL_NHL
biomarkers.clinical_use: Chlamydia psittaci association has been reported in some geographic regions, but prevalence is variable and inconsistent; doxycycline has been used in some early-stage ocular adnexal MALT lymphoma cases, while involved-site radiotherapy is a standard treatment for localized disease and rituximab-based therapy is used in selected cases

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small B lymphocytes with plasmacytic differentiation forming reactive lymphoid infiltrates in conjunctiva, lacrimal gland, or orbit

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: MALT arises in a setting of chronic antigenic stimulation with reactive follicles and monoclonal marginal zone B cells; Chlamydia psittaci association has been described in some regions but is not universal

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Marginal zone B cells recruited to conjunctival or ocular adnexal tissue through chronic antigen exposure; Chlamydia psittaci has been implicated in some geographic regions
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Marginal zone B-cell differentiation with plasmacytic maturation; typically CD20+, CD5-, CD10-, CD23-
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity:
Same MALT lymphoma biology as extranodal marginal zone lymphomas of other sites (gastric, thyroid, salivary) 
 chronic antigen stimulation drives clonal expansion
